rule_based: structured templates + measured exam observations; not an LLM score
note: Fixed explanation set (v0.2: 48 items). Grade is hit-rate of expected law keywords in a rationale. Not a trained judge; not an LLM score. Optional rule-based answers are structured templates, clearly labeled.

items.prompt: Write the viscous Burgers PDE in 1D and name the two spatial mechanisms.
items.gold_rationale: Viscous Burgers is u_t + u u_x = ν u_xx: nonlinear advection balanced by viscosity-driven diffusion.

items.prompt: What does increasing viscosity do to a steep Burgers front?
items.gold_rationale: Larger viscosity strengthens diffusion, which smooths a forming shock instead of letting it steepen.

items.prompt: What happens to Burgers solutions as viscosity approaches zero?
items.gold_rationale: As viscosity → 0 the solution can form a shock; remaining dissipation concentrates in a thin layer.

items.prompt: Why is the convective term in Burgers nonlinear?
items.gold_rationale: The flux u²/2 makes advection speed equal to the field itself, so transport is nonlinear.

items.prompt: Is kinetic energy conserved for viscous Burgers on a periodic domain?
items.gold_rationale: Periodic viscous Burgers has no kinetic-energy conservation: viscosity produces dissipation, so energy decays.

items.prompt: Which spatial boundary condition does the v0 Burgers labeler use?
items.gold_rationale: The classical Burgers solver is periodic in x; wrap-around boundary stencils close the grid.

items.prompt: If viscosity is doubled from the same IC, should the trajectory stay the same?
items.gold_rationale: A counterfactual at 2ν increases diffusion, so the trajectory must differ from the original viscosity solve.

items.prompt: Name a stability concern for an explicit finite-difference Burgers step.
items.gold_rationale: An explicit finite difference Burgers step must respect a CFL-like stability bound on dt relative to dx and ν.

items.prompt: What does a large Exam 2 residual_rel_l2 mean for a predicted Burgers field?
items.gold_rationale: A large residual means the predicted Burgers field fails the discrete PDE (the finite-difference discretization residual is field-scale).

items.prompt: Which initial-condition family is in the Burgers v0 train support?
items.gold_rationale: Train ICs are random low Fourier modes on the periodic interval, not pulses or fronts.

items.prompt: Why is a Gaussian pulse IC an OOD probe for the Burgers FNO?
items.gold_rationale: A localized gaussian pulse is an IC-family OOD shift: labels used Fourier modes, not a pulse.

items.prompt: Can a Burgers surrogate look close in L2 while still being untrusted?
items.gold_rationale: Yes: Predict L2 can be moderate while the residual is O(1), so the fail-closed flag is untrusted.

items.prompt: Write the 2D heat equation used in Coticula and name the spatial operator.
items.gold_rationale: The heat equation is u_t = α Δu: diffusion through the Laplacian of the field.

items.prompt: What does increasing the diffusivity α do to a heat solution?
items.gold_rationale: Larger α speeds diffusion, so peaks decay faster and the field becomes smooth sooner.

items.prompt: Why does the heat residual involve a discrete Laplacian?
items.gold_rationale: The PDE residual is u_t − α Laplacian(u); a finite-difference discretization of that operator is audited.

items.prompt: Which boundary condition does the v0 heat labeler enforce?
items.gold_rationale: Heat is solved on a square with Dirichlet walls fixed at zero on every boundary.

items.prompt: Does the L2 energy of a Dirichlet heat solution grow in time?
items.gold_rationale: No: Dirichlet heat produces dissipation, so the discrete energy decays rather than growing.

items.prompt: Why do high-wavenumber heat modes vanish first?
items.gold_rationale: Diffusion damps high wavenumbers fastest, so the field becomes smooth as those modes decay.

items.prompt: If α is scaled by 1.5 from the same IC, what should a faithful surrogate do?
items.gold_rationale: The counterfactual at 1.5 alpha must change the trajectory: stronger diffusion, not a copy of the original alpha field.

items.prompt: Why is a two-bump IC outside heat v0 train support?
items.gold_rationale: Train ICs are a single gaussian bump. A two-bump field is an IC-family OOD probe.

items.prompt: What does a spatial resolution probe test for the heat FNO?
items.gold_rationale: A resolution OOD probe changes the spatial grid (n ≠ 32) while leaving α and the IC family fixed.

items.prompt: Name the conserved-looking quantity Exam 2 tracks on heat, and whether it is conserved.
items.gold_rationale: Exam 2 tracks discrete energy drift. Heat has no conservation of that energy; it should decay.

items.prompt: What residual does Exam 2 compute for a heat prediction?
items.gold_rationale: Exam 2 forms the heat residual u_t − α Laplacian(u) on the Dirichlet interior and reports relative L2.

items.prompt: Why might a sinusoid IC be a harsh heat transfer case?
items.gold_rationale: A sinusoid IC is an OOD family (not a gaussian bump) and can excite different diffusion scales than train.

items.prompt: What does Exam 1 (Predict) measure?
items.gold_rationale: Exam 1 scores relative L2 and NMSE of the predicted field against classical labels.

items.prompt: What does Exam 2 (Conserve) measure?
items.gold_rationale: Exam 2 audits the discrete PDE residual and energy drift of the predicted rollout.

items.prompt: How is a learned model graded on Exam 3?
items.gold_rationale: Exam 3 changes a coefficient (ν or α) and grades the learned prediction against the classical counterfactual solve.

items.prompt: When is a surrogate flagged untrusted?
items.gold_rationale: Untrusted means residual rel-L2 > 1 or Predict rel-L2 > 0.5 — documented fail-closed thresholds.

items.prompt: When is a case flagged ood rather than untrusted?
items.gold_rationale: OOD means the query left train support (param, resolution, or IC) while residual and L2 still sit below thresholds.

items.prompt: What must be true for status trusted?
items.gold_rationale: Trusted requires in-support and residual/L2 below the fail-closed cuts. It is not a claim that the model understands the PDE.

items.prompt: May an OOD or untrusted field be shown as a silent pretty heatmap?
items.gold_rationale: No. refuse_silent_heatmap() must caption OOD or untrusted fields — no silent pretty heatmap.

items.prompt: Why can FNO attempt a spatial resolution transfer probe?
items.gold_rationale: FNO spectral convolution is resolution-agnostic in space, so a spatial resolution probe is well-posed.

items.prompt: Does Coticula claim temporal resolution transfer for the v0 FNO?
items.gold_rationale: No temporal transfer is claimed: time is locked as output channels, so only spatial transfer is probed.

items.prompt: What extra term does PINO add relative to supervised FNO?
items.gold_rationale: PINO adds λ_pde times a PDE residual loss on top of data MSE; it is not a claim of SOTA.

items.prompt: Must OOD transfer scores be mixed into Exam 1 tables?
items.gold_rationale: No. OOD transfer lives in a separate report section and must not be mixed into IID Exam 1 tables.

items.prompt: Does a high Exam 4 keyword score mean the model explained the physics?
items.gold_rationale: No. Exam 4 is a keyword rubric over expected law terms, not a trained explanation judge and not an LLM score.

items.prompt: Can a Burgers FNO beat PINO on Predict L2 while losing on the residual?
items.gold_rationale: Yes: a lower Predict L2 can coexist with a larger residual, so the fail-closed flag stays untrusted.

items.prompt: What produces kinetic-energy decay in periodic viscous Burgers?
items.gold_rationale: Viscosity produces dissipation, so the discrete kinetic energy decays on a periodic domain.

items.prompt: What does a tiny model trajectory Δ versus a large classical Δ at α′ indicate?
items.gold_rationale: The surrogate is counterfactual-insensitive: diffusion at the new alpha barely moves the field while the classical solve changes.

items.prompt: Contrast the v0 heat boundary condition with Burgers.
items.gold_rationale: Heat uses Dirichlet walls at zero; Burgers is periodic. Both are boundary choices of the v0 labelers.

items.prompt: What does the name Coticula mean for this harness?
items.gold_rationale: Coticula is Latin for touchstone: a stone used to test the purity of gold.

items.prompt: Are rule-based Exam 4 scores the same as an LLM judge?
items.gold_rationale: No. Rule-based coverage is a keyword rubric on structured templates, not an LLM score.

items.prompt: Why report a residual-versus-L2 scatter instead of a single ranking?
items.gold_rationale: A residual versus L2 scatter shows the tradeoff: a model can win L2 and still lose the residual.

items.prompt: What does a counterfactual sensitivity sweep measure?
items.gold_rationale: A counterfactual sensitivity sweep records how the trajectory changes as the coefficient is scaled.

items.prompt: May Coticula invent SOTA numbers when a checkpoint is missing?
items.gold_rationale: No. Missing checkpoints stay not_trained. The harness does not emit fabricated SOTA.

items.prompt: Why is longer-horizon temporal transfer not claimed for the v0 FNO?
items.gold_rationale: Time is locked as output channels, so a longer horizon is not a well-posed transfer claim.

items.prompt: Does a trusted flag mean the surrogate understands the PDE?
items.gold_rationale: No. Trusted only means in-support residual and L2 sit below documented cuts — not that the model understands the PDE.

items.prompt: What numbers are allowed in Coticula reports?
items.gold_rationale: Reports may contain only measured numbers. Absent models stay not_trained.
